### `items/def-cofinality.md` — CERTIFY

CURRENT TEXT READ: "**Regular and singular.** An **infinite cardinal** $\kappa$ — a cardinal ([[def-cardinal]]) with $\omega \subseteq \kappa$ ([[def-cardinal-arithmetic]]), for instance any $\aleph_\alpha$ ([[def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies]]) — is"

ASSESSMENT: The repaired clause is correct and precisely divides its three citations, with each attribution matching its target exactly:
- "a cardinal" → `def-cardinal`, which states: *"An ordinal κ ([[def-ordinal]]) is a cardinal, equivalently an initial ordinal, when no α∈κ satisfies α≈κ."* — licenses only the word "cardinal," not "infinite."
- "with ω⊆κ" → `def-cardinal-arithmetic`, which states: *"A cardinal κ is finite when κ∈ω and infinite when ω⊆κ, that is ω≤κ."* — this is the exact defining clause for "infinite," verbatim in substance, and this is the dependency A8-round-1 added to close the DeepSeek A7 rejection. It is legally present in `deps` (line 10) and legally precedes `def-cofinality` in the page's reading order (`library/foundations/cardinal-arithmetic-and-cofinality.md`: `def-cardinal-arithmetic` at item 3, `def-cofinality` at item 20).
- "for instance any ℵ_α" → `def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies`, which states: *"Every $\aleph_\alpha$ is an infinite cardinal, the operation is strictly increasing, and $\alpha \le \aleph_\alpha$; all of this is that corollary, and all of it is ZF."* — licenses exactly the example given, no more.

No citation is inflated or misattributed; the original A7 defect (attributing "infinite" to targets that never define it) is closed.

COLLATERAL: none found. Every `deps` entry (`lem-cofinality-is-well-defined`, `def-cofinal-subset-of-an-ordinal`, `def-ordinal`, `def-cardinal`, `def-cardinal-arithmetic`, `def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies`) is actually cited in the body; nothing orphaned. The remaining Remarks were re-checked with suspicion: "cf(α)=α holds only at 0, at 1, and at those ordinals that are already infinite cardinals" is a true necessary-condition claim (verified by hand for successor and countable-limit cases) and is not contradicted by singular cardinals having cf(κ)≠κ, since the remark never claims the converse. `[[thm-cofinality-basics]]` genuinely proves cf(α)≤α (clause a) and that cf of a limit ordinal is a regular infinite cardinal (clause c), backing the "singular means cf(κ)<κ" sentence. `[[thm-regularity-of-the-alephs]]` genuinely exhibits $\aleph_\omega$ as singular (clause c), backing Remark 2's citation. Title and Statement remain in step with the proof-free Definition (this is a `kind: definition` item, `proof: not-applicable`, correctly).
